note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on Tuesday 5 May 1936 and there was no contest in any division: the Unionists nominated for the 21 divisions in which they held majorities and the Nationalists for ten, and the retiring members for the divisions without a nomination were deemed re-elected (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9; Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5). Polling in County Tyrone was fixed for Wednesday 3 June 1936; no poll was needed. The new council first met on Monday 8 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 13 June 1936, p. 5). The changes printed were Glenlark (Solomon Morris for Daniel M'Crea), Bencran (Fred M'Ivor for J. M'L. Armstrong) and Gortin (H. Miles for John Turner) (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9; Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1936, p. 9); the Ulster Herald (9 May 1936, p. 5) adds Patrick Quinn for B. Donaghey and John J. Colhoun for J. A. V. Mitchell. There was no change in Sixmilecross, so the retiring member was re-nominated. Division inferred from the 31 May 1933 return (John Hutchinson, J.P.; Irish News, 19 April 1933, p. 6); John Hutchinson was appointed to the council's Carrickmore water committee on 13 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 20 June 1936, p. 3, block image read). No co-option, vacancy or by-election in the division was found in the 1936 reports read. Returned unopposed.
